rationale: Prevalence by group at one point in treatment is what a cross-sectional survey measures, and the checkbox agreement can be measured in the same respondents. Multi-mode, multilingual administration reduces the non-response bias that would hide the most affected (c3); the retrieved prevalence (c1) sets planning values; the checkbox is likely to miss many (c2). Reporting follows STROBE for cross-sectional studies.
alternatives: Longitudinal follow-up of new patients over a year (refused: the navigation decision needs prevalence now)
Adding a question to distress screening only (refused: the checkbox is what needs checking)
Trial of financial navigation (deferred: the survey decides whether and for whom)
whyNotMoreComplex: A longitudinal design or a trial would answer different questions; the survey answers the leadership's question in three months.

decision.statement: Run a cross-sectional survey of adults on systemic therapy at the centre from February to April 2027 with the validated questionnaire offered on paper, tablet and telephone in four languages, and compare the distress checkbox with the questionnaire score.
decision.question: How should the centre measure financial toxicity before deciding on a navigation service?

criteria.text: Financial toxicity is common enough elsewhere to justify local measurement, and the checkbox may miss many affected patients.
Non-response bias can be reduced by several modes and languages.
The centre has already decided on a navigation service regardless of results.

gates.requirement: Research ethics approval of the survey protocol
gates.evidence: REB-2026-204 approved 2026-09-12, supplied by the investigator
Supportive care budget line SC-2026-11, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Add a question to distress screening only
Start a navigation service without measurement
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c3 from retrieved records; both gates are met on investigator-supplied records; the quarantined lead is not used.

summary: Cross-sectional survey recommended; the decision rests on three ledger claims and both gates are met.
